ImageDescription.value: FBI Director Kash Patel testified at an oversight hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee, where lawmakers grilled him over allegations that the FBI had become more politicized under his leadership and had targeted President Trump's political opponents. Senators also questioned Mr. Patel about the bureau's decision to relax hiring standards and allegations that he sought to intimidate journalists who reported unflattering stories about him. Sen. Peter Welch (D-VT) pressed Mr. Patel on the FBI's role in the upcoming midterm elections, asking whether agents would be deployed at polling places. Mr. Patel said the FBI would have election-crimes coordinators in all 56 field offices and indicated that agents could be involved in addressing "election interference matters." He emphasized that "election integrity is of paramount importance." When asked if Mr. Trump lost the 2020 election to the winner, former President Biden, Mr. Patel declined to answer, citing ongoing investigations.
